## TL;DR

`repoos restart` restarts this repo's control-plane server on one command whether
it runs under `repoos service`, as a hand-run `repoos serve`, or under an
external supervisor such as a hand-written launchd plist with `KeepAlive`. The
round fixed the two bugs review pass 2 left open by re-deriving supervisor
detection from **real** `launchctl` output captured on this Mac, not fixtures the
tests wrote. The macOS detector now reads the tabular `launchctl list` (`PID
Status Label`) as its only positive signal, classifies an unlabelable
launchd-parented process as `uncertain` (refuse and print the manual command)
instead of `hand-run`, and derives a valid `gui/<uid>` or `system` kickstart
target from the pid's owning uid. The hand-run spawn path is wrapped,
`repoosBinary` resolves the compiled CLI entry through the shared
`compiledCliEntry` helper, and the serve lock replays the flags the server was
actually started with.

This session's work was the handoff unblock: the branch had been reset once, so
the stored round-1 report's source commit (`67b0e42a9`) was no longer an ancestor
of the branch tip and the handoff refused to compute a round-relative diff base.
I restored that history with a `-s ours` merge of the pre-reset line
(`a0608a18d`) — the tree is byte-identical to the reviewed checkpoint and
`67b0e42a9` is an ancestor again — then re-ran the scoped check green.

## Work and rationale

I reproduced the reviewer's complaint against the live machine rather than
trusting either the code or the fixtures. Three facts drove the design:

1. `launchctl list` really prints `PID\tStatus\tLabel` rows (I saw `83082 0
   com.repoos.serve.repoos-c4114ede` for this checkout, plus the reporter's
   `org.repoos.serve.kamrai`). This is a dependable signal.
2. `launchctl print pid/N` exits 0 for a nonexistent pid and its output has no
   `label =` or `domain =` line. So the old parser (requiring `label = "…"`)
   could never match a real job, and "print succeeded" proves nothing.
3. RepoOS's managed label is `com.repoos.serve.<id>`, while an external KeepAlive
   daemon has an arbitrary label such as `org.repoos.serve.kamrai` (which also
   begins `com.repoos.serve.` in lookalike cases). A prefix alone cannot decide
   managed vs external.

The rewrite (`src/core/supervisor-detect.ts`) makes `launchctl list` the only
positive *external* signal. A listed job whose label matches
`^com\.repoos\.serve\.[^.]` is the managed unit and returns `none` (the caller
uses the service manager, which the task says not to change). Any other listed
label is external, with `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/<label>` for a user pid
and `system/<label>` for root — derived from the real uid, since `gui/<label>`
without a uid is not a valid target. With no running list row the detector falls
back to parentage only: a launchd parent or ppid 1 returns `uncertain`, a plain
shell parent returns `none`. The Linux path keeps `systemctl status <pid>`
parsing, rejects the `user@<uid>.service` manager unit and slice/scope noise, and
returns `uncertain` only when the parent genuinely looks systemd-managed.

The hand-run lifecycle was tightened too. `repoosBinary` routes through
`compiledCliEntry` so the fallback resolves `dist/cli/index.js`, not
`dist/dist/cli/index.js`, and the spawned child carries an `error` listener.
`waitForPidGone`'s result is checked before any respawn, so a server that will
not exit aborts with a clear message instead of racing a second bind. Flag
replay: `serve.ts` captures restart-relevant flags into the serve lock via
`captureServeLockFlags`, `readServeLocks` surfaces them, and `restartRepoServer`
replays them, falling back to `ps`-derived argv when a lock predates
`serveFlags`. `restartHint` now names `repoos restart` for a stale server, and
`user-docs/cli.md` and `user-docs/troubleshooting.md` describe the three paths.

## Approaches tried

My first fix for the parsers kept `launchctl print pid/N` and added a `creator =
launchctl` heuristic. Live output killed that: the creator line is often absent
and a nonexistent pid still prints a block, so "creator" is neither necessary nor
sufficient. I removed the print-based classification entirely rather than pile
another guess on top.

For the unlabelable case I considered returning `external` so `restartRepoServer`
would SIGTERM and wait — what the reporter wants — but it silently restarts a
server we cannot name, and if the pid is not actually supervised, killing it
leaves nothing running. I chose `uncertain` instead: refuse and print the exact
command, trading convenience for never half-restarting an unknown process, the
failure the reviewer flagged twice. For the `--preview-overrides` class of bug I
kept the explicit `REPLAYABLE_FLAGS` allowlist rather than replaying all argv:
`--port`/`--host` are handled separately and must not duplicate, and unknown
flags could inject surprising behaviour into the respawn.

## Challenges and blockers

I cannot run a real system-domain LaunchDaemon here: this Mac has no sudo for
`nick`, and `launchctl print system/...` for the reporter's job is out of reach.
Detection is therefore proven against captured `launchctl list` / `systemctl`
output and the real rows on this machine, not against a live KeepAlive respawn.
Watching a launchd `KeepAlive` daemon actually come back on a non-sudo box
remains unverified here and should be a held human task if the reviewer wants
machine proof. Every automated test uses captured real strings.

The other blocker was procedural and worth recording. The branch had been reset
between rounds, so the reviewed round's source commit fell out of ancestry while
its report file survived on disk. The handoff's `resolveEngineeringReportBase`
then refuses with "not an ancestor of this round's source … restore the branch
history". Deleting the stale report is forbidden (reports are immutable), so the
fix is to restore the history: `git merge -s ours` the lost line into the current
tip. `-s ours` is right because the current tree already contains every file the
lost line had, so the merge restores ancestry without touching content.

One nuance worth recording: RepoOS launches serve processes through a small
launcher (`repoos-repoos … dist/cli/index.js serve …`), so `parseServeRoot` and
`verifyPidServesRepo` both read `…/cli/index.js serve`; pid verification keeps
working for supervised servers.

## Key learnings

An OS command that exits 0 for a nonexistent target is not an existence check;
`launchctl print pid/N` is exactly that, so supervision detection must key off
`launchctl list` rows and parentage, never off "print succeeded". Managed vs
external cannot be decided by a prefix alone, because `com.repoos.serve.` covers
both this tool's units and hand-written lookalikes — it needs the full label
shape and, when in doubt, a refusal. And any restart that stops before it starts
owes the user a synchronous, printed manual command at every point it can fail;
`repoos restart` now returns one for the timeout, the spawn failure, and the
uncertain-supervisor case alike.

A resettled branch is recoverable without losing reviewed work, but only by
restoring ancestry, not by editing reports: the round-relative diff base is the
previous report's `sourceSha`, so that commit must stay an ancestor of every
later tip.
